issues.t: Water pump fails and leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping with no visible leak, milky or tan oil on the dipstick, white exhaust smoke, overheating, or a sudden engine failure.
issues.why: On the V6, the water pump sits inside the engine and is driven by the timing chain. When its seal fails, coolant can leak straight into the oil, which ruins the engine bearings. Owners report this most often around 90,000 to 140,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and look at the oil for a milky color. If coolant is going missing, stop driving and have a shop pressure test it right away. Many owners replace the water pump and timing chain as preventive work around 100,000 miles.

issues.t: Brake booster fails and the pedal goes hard
issues.sym: The brake pedal becomes very hard to push and the vehicle takes much more effort and distance to stop. You may hear a hiss from under the dash.
issues.why: The vacuum brake booster that adds power to the pedal can fail. It is the most reported problem on these years, and Mazda once offered extended coverage that has now ended.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. A hard brake pedal means the brake assist has failed, so the car needs much more force and distance to stop. If it happens while driving, press the pedal firmly, slow down and pull off the road when it's safe. Don't keep driving it: have it towed to a shop. Replacing the booster is usually a straightforward repair.

issues.t: Sudden loss of braking
issues.sym: The pedal feels hard or goes long and the vehicle does not slow as expected.
issues.why: Owners of 2014 CX-9s reported sudden braking loss, often traced to the power brake booster.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Do not keep driving with poor brakes. Have the booster, vacuum supply and brake fluid checked right away.

issues.t: Cylinder head can crack and leak coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping, a sweet smell, the warning "High engine temperature / engine output may be limited," overheating, or white exhaust smoke.
issues.why: Owners of the 2.5L turbo report cracks in the cylinder head that let coolant leak out, sometimes into the engine. Repairs are major, and some engines were replaced.
issues.next: Check the coolant level regularly. If it keeps dropping or the temperature warning appears, stop and have the cooling system pressure tested before driving further.

issues.t: Radiator leaks from the top
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crust at the top of the radiator, and the coolant level slowly drops.
issues.why: Owners report the plastic top tank of the radiator cracking and leaking.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and get the radiator replaced before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Brakes wear out early
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing and pads and rotors needing replacement at low mileage, sometimes under 20,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners of the 2016 model report unusually fast brake pad and rotor wear.
issues.next: Have brake thickness measured at each oil change. Ask the dealer about updated pads if they wear out quickly.

issues.t: Click or squeak from the front brakes
issues.sym: A click or squeak from the front brakes, often at low speed or when changing direction.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for 2016-2022 CX-9s covering front brake clicks and squeaks, fixed by servicing the pads and their hardware.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the bulletin; it is a noise issue rather than a safety one, but have the brakes inspected.

issues.t: Mazda Connect screen freezes, ghost touches or won't start
issues.sym: The infotainment screen freezes, reboots, stays blank, or responds to touches you did not make. Radio, navigation or phone features may stop working.
issues.why: Owners have reported faults with the Mazda Connect system since 2016, and Mazda released bulletins for screens that stay blank or are slow to start.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest Mazda Connect software. If the screen acts on its own, the display may need replacing.

issues.t: Satellite radio resets or will not connect
issues.sym: SiriusXM radio keeps resetting, drops out, or will not connect.
issues.why: Owners of the 2019 CX-9 report the satellite radio repeatedly losing its connection.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for an infotainment software update and to check the antenna connection.

issues.t: Paint flaking off
issues.sym: Paint chipping or peeling at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners of the 2019 model report paint flaking from body panels.
issues.next: Photograph the damage and ask the dealer about paint warranty coverage while the vehicle is still new.

issues.t: Creaking from the suspension
issues.sym: A creaking noise over bumps or when turning, even at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners of the 2017 model reported suspension creaks early in ownership.
issues.next: Have the dealer check sway bar bushings and strut mounts while the vehicle is under warranty.

issues.t: Creak or clunk from the steering column
issues.sym: Creaking, knocking or a clunk from the steering column, especially on rough roads.
issues.why: Mazda bulletins trace this to a nut in the steering column that can loosen. An owner told NHTSA the dealer confirmed a loose bolt on a 2022.
issues.next: Have it checked soon; the dealer can tighten or replace the parts under the bulletin.

issues.t: Rattle or pop from the cowl at the base of the windshield
issues.sym: A rattle, clunk or pop from the front of the vehicle near the windshield.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for loose cowl panel bolts, and an owner reported several loose windshield header and cowl bolts on a 2022.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check and tighten the cowl panel bolts.

issues.t: Low oil warning with code P250F
issues.sym: A low engine oil warning or check engine light, sometimes with the oil level actually fine.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for the low oil level warning with code P250F, and a separate one for high oil consumption.
issues.next: Check the dipstick first. If the level is correct, ask the dealer about the bulletin; if it is low, have oil consumption tested.

issues.t: Battery runs down when the seat ventilation is left on
issues.sym: A weak or dead battery after the vehicle sits.
issues.why: Mazda bulletins note that seat ventilation left switched on can drain the battery, and give battery testing steps.
issues.next: Turn seat ventilation off before parking. If the battery keeps dying, have it tested and checked for a drain.

issues.t: Power liftgate opens by itself
issues.sym: The power liftgate opens on its own while parked or stopped.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin covering power liftgates that can open unintentionally.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the bulletin repair. Be careful at drive-throughs and garages until it is fixed.

issues.t: A/C weak because outside temperature reads too low
issues.sym: The outside temperature display reads about 10°C (18°F) lower than it really is, and the A/C or climate control does not cool or hold temperature well.
issues.why: Mazda bulletins trace this to the ambient temperature sensor or its software.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the bulletin; the fix is usually a sensor or software update.

issues.t: Seat heater overheats
issues.sym: A seat heater gets very hot, burns skin, or smokes or scorches the seat.
issues.why: Owners have filed federal complaints about seat heaters overheating, including one that burned a hole in the seat.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater if it feels too hot or you smell burning, and have the dealer inspect the seat heater element and control.

issues.t: Brake pedal sinks or braking feels weak
issues.sym: The brake pedal sinks nearly to the floor or the vehicle does not slow as expected.
issues.why: Several owners filed federal complaints about poor braking on the 2023 CX-9, including one that needed several repair attempts.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Do not keep driving with a sinking pedal. Have the brake fluid, master cylinder and booster checked right away and report it to NHTSA.

issues.t: Power steering thud or loss of assist
issues.sym: A thud from the steering wheel, heavy steering, or the steering briefly not responding.
issues.why: Owners filed federal complaints about electric power steering faults, including a failed bearing.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have the steering inspected right away if it feels heavy or makes a thud.

issues.t: Repeated vehicle malfunction alerts
issues.sym: Many warning messages such as "Critical Vehicle Malfunction," slow starts, or controls not responding.
issues.why: Owners report software faults on the 2023 CX-9. Mazda bulletins also cover a network malfunction message and master warning light.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest software updates and have the battery tested, since low voltage can trigger many warnings.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: There is usually no warning. The danger only shows up in a crash.
issues.why: The passenger airbag inflator can rupture after years of heat and humidity, throwing metal pieces into the cabin. Mazda told owners of unrepaired vehicles not to drive them, and some earlier replacement inflators were recalled too.
issues.next: Check your VIN today. If the recall is open, do not drive it; ask a Mazda dealer to tow it in for the free repair.

issues.t: Front lower ball joints can corrode and separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, loose or wandering steering.
issues.why: Water can get into the front lower ball joints and rust them until the control arm separates, which can cause a loss of control.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers replace both front lower control arms free.

issues.t: Power seat wiring can short (recall)
issues.sym: The power seat stops working or moves on its own, or there is a burning smell under the seat.
issues.why: On seats with memory, the wiring under the cushion can rub on a bracket and short.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free inspection and repair.

issues.t: Light bulb socket harness melts
issues.sym: A light stops working, and the socket or wiring is melted or scorched.
issues.why: Owners of the 2009 CX-9 report melted bulb harnesses.
issues.next: Replace the damaged socket and wiring, not just the bulb, or the new bulb may fail too.

issues.t: Sunroof leaks water
issues.sym: Water drips into the cabin from around the sunroof, for example in a car wash.
issues.why: Owners report sunroof leaks, usually from clogged or loose drain tubes.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and checked before water damages the headliner or wiring.

issues.t: Seat heater can overheat in extreme cold (recall)
issues.sym: A seat heater that gets very hot, smoke, or a burning smell.
issues.why: In extreme cold, the seat heater control circuit can overheat, which could burn an occupant or start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free repair.

issues.t: Front strut bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension or the steering pulling.
issues.why: Lower strut mounting bolts can loosen, letting the steering knuckle separate from the strut.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free repair.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Hesitation, rough running, stalling or a no-start.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump impeller can crack and swell, so the pump fails.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If it stalls, get to a safe spot and have it towed. Dealers replace the pump free.

issues.t: Wiring connector fault can disable airbag or starting (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light, turn signals that work only sometimes, or the engine not starting.
issues.why: Weak connector retention in a wiring harness can break communication between modules.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free harness repair.

issues.t: Tire tread can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration, a bulge in the tread, or a sudden tire failure.
issues.why: Some tires were made with the wrong rubber compound, so the tread can separate.
issues.next: Check your VIN and the tires; dealers replace affected tires free.

issues.t: Second-row seat can slide forward in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: The left second-row seat may not feel firmly locked on its track.
issues.why: On 60/40 second-row benches, the left seat can slide forward in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free seat repair.
